newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says Thailand mulling Natuna pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Thailand mulling Natuna pipeline.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina said on Wednesday the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) has promised to study the feasibility of a pipeline linking Thailand to the giant Natuna gas field.

"Pertamina and PTT agreed on August 21 in Bangkok to discuss further a natural gas pipeline from Natuna. We will have another meeting, possibly at the end of this month in Indonesia, at which PTT is expected to give a response," Yaved Sumbung, Pertamina's chief of liquefied natural gas, told reporters.
"Pertamina has said it can't compete with countries near Thailand, such as Myanmar or Malaysia, on gas prices," he added.
"What we can offer from Natuna is security of long-term gas supply. PTT has indicated it needs around 960 million standard cubic feet a day of gas," Sumbung added.
Sumbung said Pertamina has also offered Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, gas from the Natuna field in the South China Sea.

Indonesia signed an agreement in late 1994 with U.S. oil firm Exxon Corp to exploit the Natuna field, which contains an estimated 210 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of gas, of which 45 Tcf are thought to be recoverable commercially.
Pertamina owns 24 percent of the Natuna project, Mobil Corp 26 percent and Exxon 50 percent.
Gas from the field is expected to start flowing by 2003/2004.
